en.title: BioWare Documentary Becomes a Touching Farewell After Studio's Closure
en.summary: A documentary chronicling the storied history of **BioWare** was already two years into production when Electronic Arts announced the studio's closure. Now, 'Massive Effect: The BioWare Story' is poised to serve as a poignant elegy for the beloved developer.
en.body:
## A Documentary's Unforeseen Ending

Filming for **Massive Effect: The BioWare Story**, a Canadian documentary delving into the 31-year history of the iconic game developer, was well underway when **EA** made the devastating announcement of **BioWare**'s closure. The film, which had been in production for two years, was intended to celebrate the studio's rich legacy, but its narrative has now taken a profound and somber turn. Writer and director **Akash Sherman** described the founders as "hometown heroes" and expressed the weight of documenting the journey of "underdogs who came together to create deeply beloved storytelling."

> "With the studio's recent closure, the film is now a profound valediction."

The documentary promises an in-depth look at **BioWare**'s evolution, featuring interviews with key figures from its past and present. Among those interviewed are founders **Ray Muzyka**, **Greg Zeschuk**, and **Augustine Yip**, alongside influential developers such as **Casey Hudson**, **Mark Darrah**, **David Gaider**, and **Drew Karpyshyn**. Voice actor **Jennifer Hale**, known for her iconic role as Commander Shepard, and former **EA** CEO **John Riccitello** are also set to appear, offering a comprehensive perspective on the studio's impact.

## A Legacy Remembered

The closure of **BioWare** marks the end of an era for many gamers who grew up with titles like **Mass Effect** and **Dragon Age**. While the studio's peak popularity spanned the late 2000s and early 2010s, its influence on the RPG genre is undeniable, with fans cherishing nearly every game it produced, even those with controversial receptions like **Mass Effect: Andromeda**. The cancellation of a new **Mass Effect** game, which was in development at the time of the shutdown, adds another layer of tragedy to the studio's final chapter. The documentary aims to honor the talent and passion that fueled **BioWare**'s creations, ensuring their stories and characters continue to resonate.

> "BioWare was never just about the logo or the building. It was about deeply emotionally engaging stories and characters, brought to life by the amazingly talented people on our dev teams, and our excellent production and distribution partners who helped us bring those stories successfully to all corners of the planet, and our passionate fans who defended those worlds, championed them and carried them forward."

**Ray Muzyka** and **Greg Zeschuk** shared their thoughts on the film, stating, "When the production team asked for our blessing to tell the BioWare story, we were honored and genuinely moved." They emphasized that the studio's essence lay in its stories and the people who crafted them, a sentiment the film is poised to capture.

## What's Next

**Massive Effect: The BioWare Story** is slated for release next year, offering fans a chance to reflect on and celebrate the enduring legacy of **BioWare**. The documentary is expected to provide a final, intimate look at a studio that shaped the hearts and minds of a generation of gamers.

content_raw: Deadline reports that a Canadian documentary about the history of BioWare was already two years into filming when EA closed the studio. Now, it's becoming a sad goodbye to a legendary developer. "The BioWare founders are my hometown heroes," the documentary's writer and director Akash Sherman said. "It's a privilege and responsibility to share the journey of underdogs who came together to create deeply beloved storytelling. Their golden era kindled a spark in me and in an entire generation. With the studio's recent closure, the film is now a profound valediction." The documentary, Massive Effect: The BioWare Story, features interviews with the studio's founders, Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk, and Augustine Yip, as well as developers Casey Hudson, Mark Darrah, David Gaider, Drew Karpyshyn, Aaryn Flynn, Mac Walters, Trent Oster, James Ohlen, and Caroline Livingstone, voice actor Jennifer Hale, former CEO of EA John Riccitello, and vice president of Lucasfilm Games Douglas Reilly. "When the production team asked for our blessing to tell the BioWare story, we were honored and genuinely moved," Muzyka and Zeschuk said in a statement. "BioWare was never just about the logo or the building. It was about deeply emotionally engaging stories and characters, brought to life by the amazingly talented people on our dev teams, and our excellent production and distribution partners who helped us bring those stories successfully to all corners of the planet, and our passionate fans who defended those worlds, championed them and carried them forward. We're proud this film honors those who made it all possible. The best stories never really end. They live on in our memories and wait for someone to pick them up again." Massive Effect: The BioWare Story is scheduled for release next year. Meanwhile, composer Sam Hulick has shared a re-scored version of the leaked trailer for Mass Effect Universe as his own way of saying goodbye, though apparently Amazon's Mass Effect TV series is still in the works .
